tagline: A weekly letter on the sentences you missed
audience: Readers 28-55 who still subscribe to literary journals. Slow-paced, print-aware, value craft over volume.

copy.HERO_HEADLINE: Sentences worth keeping, every Sunday morning
copy.HERO_LEDE: Threadbare is a weekly newsletter about prose, attention, and the quiet craft of writing. One short essay every Sunday — the kind you'd finish on the bus before your stop.
copy.HERO_TRUST: Read by 6,400 writers and stubborn readers · Issue 142 lands this Sunday
copy.RECENT_LEDE: Six minutes a week, roughly. Always one essay, never a roundup.
copy.RECENT_1_TITLE: On the sentence that won't end
copy.RECENT_1_SUB: What the long sentence asks of the reader, and why I keep writing them anyway. With detours through Cusk, Hazzard, and a wet morning in March.
copy.RECENT_2_SUB: On choosing the notebook over the dashboard, even when the dashboard is winning. A quiet defence of writing for an audience of one.
copy.RECENT_3_TITLE: What I learned from a year of bad first drafts
copy.RECENT_3_SUB: Twelve months of letting myself write badly. Forty-eight essays, three I'd reread, one I will. The maths I didn't expect.
copy.PULL_QUOTE: The only newsletter I leave unread on purpose, because I want to save it for Sunday.
copy.PULL_QUOTE_ATTR: — A reader, in a kind email
copy.SUBSCRIBE_LEDE: Free for everyone. A pay-what-you-want tier supports the time it takes to write something thinkable.
copy.SUBSCRIBE_DISCLAIMER: One letter on Sundays. Unsubscribe at any time, no hard feelings.
copy.ABOUT_HEADLINE: Hello, I'm the writer behind Threadbare
copy.ABOUT_LEDE: I'm Lina, a writer based in a small flat in Edinburgh. Threadbare is the letter I wished existed when I was learning to write — quiet, weekly, and indifferent to the algorithm.
copy.ABOUT_BODY: Threadbare started in early 2023 as an experiment. I wanted to write one essay a week — small, fixed in scope, finishable on a Sunday morning — and see if anyone wanted to read them. Three years later it's the project I'm proudest of. Most weeks I write about prose: the long sentence, the unfinished thought, the moment a paragraph turns. Sometimes I write about the city, or about reading itself, or about the strange small failures of the writing life. I try to keep it short enough to read in one sitting and long enough to leave a mark. If you've found your way here, thank you. The letter is free. There's a pay-what-you-want tier for readers who'd like to support the time it takes to write something thinkable, but I genuinely don't mind which side of that you land on. Either way, I'm glad you're reading.
copy.ARCHIVE_LEDE: From the first letter in February 2023. Newest first.
